label: D1 after a rewarded a2 trial, late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the agent will repeat a2
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), almost exclusively when the reward input is 1 (99.9% of mass) and the previous choice was a2 (prev_action==1 holds 0.2% of mass; prev_action -1 is just the first trial in the window, where the choice is not visible). The agent then chooses a2 again (next GO choice a2 in >99.9% of activations; action at D1 is the agent own upcoming choice, which it can compute, not a random future outcome). It also depends strongly on episode time: zero activations before ep_trial ~55, then the rate rises from trial 60 to 99 (an episode-clock component). The policy logit at D1 is moderately negative (favours a2) and value is low/moderate. Magnitude is larger across a run of consecutive rewarded a2 trials (example windows climb 0.1 -> 1.0 over a streak) and in good=S2 / start_high episodes. Not active after unrewarded trials, after a1 choices, or early in the episode. Without the upcoming-choice term (observed variables only) F1 drops to 0.75 (precision 0.62), because of D1s after a rewarded a2 where the agent then switches to a1. Dev: P 0.75, R 0.95, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.996. The ep_trial threshold is approximate, since activation ramps up through trials 60-70.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the predicate includes D1 steps after a RARE-rewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S1, rewarded). Adding (prev_common == 0) to the recorded predicate gives 5506 predicted test rows with 0 activations (precision 0.0). This is the model-based distinction the task is built around, and the label and explanation leave it out.

The same holds from the reached-state side. in_rew==1 & prev_state==2 & prev_action==1 (a rare-rewarded a1 trial that reached S2) gives precision 0.02 and mass recall 0.003. So the feature needs a2 + common + rewarded, not just 'rewarded a2' and not just 'rewarded at S2'.

Restricting to common previous transitions (prev_state in {-1, 2} & prev_common != 0) and keeping action==2 & ep_trial>=65 lifts test F1 from 0.825 to 0.884 (precision 0.73 -> 0.83, recall unchanged at 0.948, mass recall 0.995).
The observed-only version improves too: test F1 0.733 -> 0.795 when common-only is used in place of prev_action != 1.

prev_action == -1 (the window's first trial, where the previous choice is hidden) holds about 22% of activation mass. With prev_action == 2 strictly, mass recall falls to 0.78. The explanation treats this as trivial, but it is a large share of the mass, and the claim that the previous choice was a2 cannot be checked for that share.
Claims that check out: D1 only (phase != D1 has 0 activations); requires in_rew == 1; a1-common-rewarded trials give 0 activations; the upcoming choice is almost always a2.

Streak effect confirmed: many remaining false positives are the first rewarded trial after an unrewarded one. Adding tv('reward',-2) != 0 raises precision to 0.886 but lowers recall (F1 0.869), so the streak dependence is graded.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a COMMON-rewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S2, rewarded; never after rare a2 -> S1 rewards), late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the agent will repeat a2; grows over a rewarded streak
